paper_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What are the primary reasons for selecting PTB7 as the donor polymer instead of P3HT for all-polymer solar cells using P(NDI2OD-T2) as the acceptor?
qa_pairs.answer: PTB7 was selected because it possesses a deeper highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level than P3HT, which is expected to enable higher open-circuit voltages. Additionally, PTB7 has a more red-shifted absorption spectrum compared to P3HT, allowing for better utilization of the solar spectrum.
qa_pairs.source_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What are the photovoltaic performance metrics, including PCE, JSC, VOC, and fill factor, for the optimized PTB7:P(NDI2OD-T2) solar cell?
qa_pairs.answer: The optimized PTB7:P(NDI2OD-T2) all-polymer solar cell achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 1.1%, a short-circuit current (JSC) of 3.4 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.62 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 0.39.
qa_pairs.source_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: How does the external quantum efficiency (EQE) of the PTB7:P(NDI2OD-T2) blend characterize its spectral response?
qa_pairs.answer: The PTB7:P(NDI2OD-T2) blend exhibits a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 18% at a wavelength of 680 nm, indicating its most efficient charge generation occurs in the red region of the spectrum.
qa_pairs.source_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: Contrast the crystallinity and molecular orientation of PTB7 and P(NDI2OD-T2) when they are blended together.
qa_pairs.answer: In the blend, P(NDI2OD-T2) forms face-on oriented crystallites, whereas the PTB7 donor matrix remains essentially amorphous. This indicates that only the acceptor polymer maintains a high degree of structural order within the mixture.
qa_pairs.source_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: According to Scherrer analysis and GIWAXS data, how does blending with PTB7 impact the crystallite thickness and d-spacing of P(NDI2OD-T2)?
qa_pairs.answer: Blending with PTB7 reduces the P(NDI2OD-T2) crystallite thickness along the (100) direction from 19 nm (in neat films) to 9.5 nm. Furthermore, the d-spacing of the P(NDI2OD-T2) (100) peak shifts from approximately 2.4 nm in neat films to 2.3 nm in the blend, suggesting a more compact lamellar packing.
qa_pairs.source_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What does NEXAFS spectroscopy reveal about the vertical phase separation at the top surface of the PTB7:P(NDI2OD-T2) active layer?
qa_pairs.answer: NEXAFS spectroscopy in Auger electron yield (AEY) mode shows that the top ~1 nm surface of the blend is enriched with the acceptor polymer, containing approximately 68 wt% P(NDI2OD-T2) compared to the 1:1 bulk ratio.
qa_pairs.source_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: Based on scanning transmission X-ray microscopy (STXM) results, what can be concluded about the mesoscale morphology of PTB7:P(NDI2OD-T2) blends?
qa_pairs.answer: STXM imaging indicates a lack of mesoscale phase separation in PTB7:P(NDI2OD-T2) blends, as no morphological features larger than the 30 nm X-ray beam spot size were detectable.
qa_pairs.source_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What are the optimal processing conditions, including solvent, weight ratio, and thickness, for fabricating PTB7:P(NDI2OD-T2) active layers?
qa_pairs.answer: The optimal active layer is approximately 70 nm thick, processed from a 1:1 weight ratio solution of PTB7 and P(NDI2OD-T2) in anhydrous chlorobenzene.
qa_pairs.source_title: All-Polymer Solar Cells Utilizing Low Band Gap Polymers as Donor and Acceptor
